title: The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0: Core Specification
note: Your Drive had version 15.0; this page follows version 18.0, whose PDF was downloaded from unicode.org into the same folder. Since 16.0 the core specification is also published as authoritative HTML, so every chapter and numbered section links to its place there as well as to its PDF pages. Summaries and terms are per chapter. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: The core specification of Unicode: the architecture, conformance rules and implementation guidance for the universal character encoding, followed by script-by-script descriptions of how each writing system is encoded and should be rendered. The first chapters define code points, encoding forms (UTF-8/16/32), normalization, character properties, bidirectional and boundary behavior, and implementation practices. Chapters 7–20 survey the world’s scripts by region, from Latin and Greek through West Asian, Indic and Southeast Asian scripts (including Kannada and the other Brahmic scripts), East Asian ideographs and Hangul, African and American scripts; later chapters cover notational systems, symbols and format characters, and how the code charts are organized.
